title: Electricity cost calculations sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 24 (Electricity cost calculations sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 24: Paying for electricity: kilowatt-hours and cost. To understand how energy used by appliances is measured in kilowatt-hours and how to calculate its cost

model.title: A 2 kW heater runs for 3 hours at 25p per kWh. Find the cost.

questions.q: A 3 kW kettle runs for 4 minutes. Energy in kWh? Cost at 25p per kWh?
questions.model: Convert time to hours: 4 ÷ 60 = 0.0667 h (one fifteenth). Energy = 3 × 0.0667 = 0.2 kWh. Cost = 0.2 × 25p = 5p.

questions.q: A 0.1 kW TV is on for 5 hours. Energy?
Cost of 12 kWh at 25p per kWh?
Core: Use your appliance table. Estimate how long each is used per day and calculate daily kWh and cost (25p per kWh as the example price).
questions.a: Pupils' own; e.g. kettle 3 kW × 0.2 h = 0.6 kWh = 15p.
questions.model: Teacher does the kettle first: 3 kW, about 12 minutes a day = 0.2 h; 0.6 kWh; 0.6 × 25 = 15p.

questions.q: Extend: A meter read 14 562 kWh last month and 14 832 kWh this month. Cost at 25p per kWh?
Stretch: Suggest three changes to cut your family's electricity cost and estimate the saving for one.
questions.a: For example: replace 5 old 60 W bulbs with 8 W LEDs used 4 h a day: saves 5 × 0.052 × 4 = 1.04 kWh a day, about 26p a day.

questions.q: Big question: how much does it cost to boil a kettle?
questions.a: About 5p for a 4-minute boil of a 3 kW kettle at 25p per kWh.
